newsitem.title: USA: Orange County, Calif, board failed to approve tender.
newsitem.headline: Orange County, Calif, board failed to approve tender.

text.p: The Orange County, Calif., Board of Supervisors on Tuesday failed to approve a proposed tender offer of taxable refunding pension obligation bonds, a county spokeswoman said.
The county board voted 4-to-1 to continue the agenda item for one month without taking any action on the proposal at Tuesday's meeting, according to spokeswoman Diane Thomas.
On Monday, the county's Public Finance Advisory Committee approved the proposal, which called for the county to sell about $130 million of debt to refund outstanding 1994 Series A pension bonds.

Had the county Board of Supervisors approved the proposal Tuesday, county advisers said they would have moved quickly to issue $129.7 million of the refunding bonds to complete the restructuring of the pension obligation bonds.
The county said on Monday that it had received tender offers from about 63 percent of the bondholders, representing about $120 million of the outstanding bonds.
The county said the tender offer would provide much-needed budget relief in the near-term, and would result in a net present-value savings of about $2.5 million.
